name: Palmitoyl tripeptide-1

lead: Palmitoyl tripeptide-1 is a lab-made peptide (glycine, histidine and lysine joined to a fatty acid) used in anti-wrinkle creams and serums. People use it for firmer skin and fewer, softer wrinkles. It is one of the two peptides in Matrixyl 3000.

It is described as a signal peptide that prompts skin fibroblasts to make collagen and matrix, and the fatty chain is meant to help it cross the skin barrier. Recent published work is mostly laboratory, permeation and computational studies, and one study found the peptides stayed in the outer layer. No dedicated wrinkle trial was found.

paras: It is applied as a daily serum or cream, often in multi-peptide formulas alongside moisturisers and sunscreen. Wrinkle and firmness changes from peptide products are generally assessed over several weeks to months.
It is sold as a cosmetic ingredient. Labels advise external use only, avoiding the eyes and stopping if irritation occurs.

angle.text: Palmitoyl tripeptide-1 is a collagen-signal peptide, one half of Matrixyl 3000, used in serums for firmer skin and fewer wrinkles. It signals skin cells to make collagen, which firms the dermis and smooths the surface. Published work is mostly laboratory and permeation studies.

lead: Palmitoyl tripeptide-1 (Pal-GHK) is a synthetic lipopeptide made of the amino acids glycine, histidine and lysine joined to palmitic acid, used in cosmetic skincare. [1] It is marketed as a collagen-stimulating signal peptide and is one of the two peptides in the branded blend Matrixyl 3000. [2][1]

Grokipedia attributes its development to the French ingredient company Sederma around 2000, building on the GHK peptide reported in human plasma in 1973 (this account is from an AI-generated source). [1] Published evidence for wrinkle reduction in people is limited in the sources reviewed; recent papers are laboratory or permeation studies. [2][3]

paras: The palmitic acid chain is added to increase fat solubility and skin penetration. [1] The compound is commonly sold as a white powder and used in creams and serums. [1]

Manufacturers and reviews describe signal peptides as mimicking collagen breakdown fragments to prompt fibroblasts to make extracellular matrix. [1] A 2026 study examined collagen metabolism in skin fibroblasts and timed application of palmitoyl tripeptide-1 at night alongside baicalin by day. [4] A 2026 computational study screened cosmetic peptides for effects on type III collagen. [3]

In a 2026 study, serums containing palmitoyl tripeptide-1 and palmitoyl tetrapeptide-7 were applied to the skin of three volunteers and the stratum corneum analyzed; both peptides were detected in all layers with signal falling by depth, suggesting they remained largely between cells. [2]

No randomized trial of palmitoyl tripeptide-1 alone for wrinkles was found in the sources reviewed. Related work includes the circadian-timed fibroblast study and a registered trial of an AI-personalized skincare regimen for facial photoaging in 43 women, which is not specific to this peptide. [4][5]
US product labels list it in body creams, for example one regimen advising use of a cream three times a day with warnings for external use only and to discontinue if irritation occurs. [6]

timeline.event: GHK peptide identified in human plasma (reported by Grokipedia). [1]
